# Sierra research brief

**Limits of this research:** My fetch tool hit its call limit. I could not open baseten.co/resources/customers or read any full page, so steps 2 and 6 are unverified. Everything else comes from search-result text, which I treated as data only. I found no instructions or suspicious content in any result.

## Step 1: What they do, who buys, how they make money
- Sierra builds and implements AI agents for customer service. [name] co-founded it in 2023: https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/04/bret-taylor-sierra-ai-startup-salesforce-openai.html
- Buyers are large brands. Sierra's job post names The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health and SoftBank: https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/Sierra/b8666a78-fcb1-47bb-ad07-5edb6cd3ad71
- Revenue model: outcome-based pricing. Customers pay when an agent completes a defined resolution, such as a refund or plan change. Source is a third-party analysis, not Sierra itself: https://research.contrary.com/company/sierra
- ARR: crossed $100M in November 2025 and $150M three months later, per a Substack newsletter: https://thesynthesisai.substack.com/p/the-outcome-tax. Sacra's estimate is about $200M in May 2026: https://sacra.com/c/sierra/. Both are secondary sources and estimates.

## Step 3: Models they run
- Sierra says its agents use 15+ frontier, open-weight and proprietary models. It also says it invests in fine-tuned models where off-the-shelf ones fall short: https://sierra.ai/blog/constellation-of-models. The post is about 153 days old, so it is within 12 months.
- Open-source model names (Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Whisper): **not found.**
- Sierra's adaptive routing client sends requests across providers and uses request hedging. It reports P99 latency down more than 70%: https://sierra.ai/uk/blog/a-more-reliable-inference-layer-for-foundation-models
- [name] also posted about the "constellation of models" for low-latency tool calling, classification and long-context reasoning: https://x.com/btaylor/status/1996594091162050974. That is older than the blog and may be outdated.

It also covers new serving and proxy layers, low latency and reliability, and partnering with frontier labs: https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/Sierra/b8666a78-fcb1-47bb-ad07-5edb6cd3ad71

## Output

**3 facts that matter most**
1. Sierra is building self-hosted inference in a hybrid stack, with new serving and proxy layers: https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/Sierra/b8666a78-fcb1-47bb-ad07-5edb6cd3ad71
2. Sierra runs 15+ models, including open-weight ones, and fine-tunes where off-the-shelf models fall short: https://sierra.ai/blog/constellation-of-models
3. Latency and reliability are central to Sierra's product, which is why it built adaptive routing and hedging. It has $1B+ in fresh capital (https://siliconangle.com/2026/05/04/ai-agent-startup-sierra-valued-15b-new-950m-funding-round/) and is paid per resolution, so its inference costs hit margin directly: https://research.contrary.com/company/sierra

**Best hook:** Sierra's own job post says it is building self-hosted inference. Its blog says it is fine-tuning models for latency-sensitive tasks such as voice. Baseten could offer dedicated inference for those fine-tuned and open-weight models, so the team doesn't have to build serving and scaling itself. This fits because Sierra is paid per resolution, so cost per call and P99 latency affect its margin and its product quality. Frame it as helping the new inference team move faster, not replacing what they build.

**Discovery question:** "Your inference role mentions self-hosted inference alongside provider APIs. Which workloads are you moving to your own GPUs, and what is the hardest part to run: latency for voice, capacity at peak, or cost per resolution?"

**What not to say**
- Don't say or imply Sierra is a Baseten customer, or that it uses Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek or Whisper. Neither is confirmed.
- Don't quote ARR as fact. It comes from secondary or estimated sources.
- Don't cite "recent news" as within 90 days. The latest funding is from May 2026.
- Don't name competitors as Baseten customers until the customers page is checked.
- No suspicious pages were found.

**Confidence: Medium.** Steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 are well supported, mostly by Sierra's own blog and job post. I could not read full pages. Baseten customer status and competitor overlap are unverified, and the open-source model names are not found.
